risk_note: RV2, settlement only (credit-order guard, rebate port decision, worker wiring, a one-off CLI); no migration, no contract change, no money moves (withdraw lane, model Claude Opus 5.5; orchestrator rulings D10-923, D10-924, D10-930). Before this task a jd order left fully refunded while orders.jd.refunded_quantity_r9_enabled was off stayed WAITING after the switch went on whenever the union report did not change (orders' content_hash short circuit), so the monthly batch credited it. Now (1) the single-order credit (R5), after its step-2 checks under the order key lock, voids such an order through the same decision as B2-04zzg (PLATFORM_INVALID through the generated transition, VOID with reason REFUND, history source system, order.invalidated on the same transaction, no voucher, no order.credited) and skips the batch item with jd_remaining_zero_void; with the switch off it credits as before with one warn; (2) a CLI lists such orders by default and voids them with --apply (needs --actor), one transaction per order under the order key lock, re-reading and skipping an order that no longer qualifies, writing an audit_logs row; a failing order rolls back alone and the CLI exits 1. Real risks: voiding a jd order whose counts are unknown (covered: #11), voiding on a partial refund (#5), voiding a credited or already VOID order (#7, #8), a stale CLI candidate (#12), a partial write when the publish or audit fails (#6, #13), cross-app effects (#8). Test-machine full verify not run (AWS runners disabled, D10-555; CI verify-int is the full verification); red and implementation runs in the local Docker container / host slot.
